audience.text: Python developers building tools that parse, inspect, modify, and serialize HTML documents using WHATWG DOM and CSSOM APIs.

capabilities.text: Parse HTML strings, fragments, and files into a DOM tree using HTMLDocument.parse, HTMLDocument.parse_fragment, and HTMLDocument.load.
capabilities.title: Parse HTML into DOM

capabilities.text: Create, append, and remove nodes; read/write attributes, text content, and classes; traverse with NodeList, TreeWalker, NodeIterator, and Range.
capabilities.title: DOM manipulation and traversal

capabilities.text: Attach CSS stylesheets, inspect rule types like CSSStyleRule and CSSMediaRule, and resolve computed styles via ComputedStyleDeclaration.
capabilities.title: CSSOM and computed styles

capabilities.text: Parse and manipulate URLs with URL and URLSearchParams; detect encoding from bytes using detect_encoding.
capabilities.title: URL and encoding utilities

capabilities.text: Execute JavaScript against a parsed DOM using JSContext backed by QuickJS, with module registration support.
capabilities.title: Optional JavaScript execution

capabilities.text: Drive the WHATWG-compliant tokenizer and tree builder directly via Tokenizer and TreeBuilder for low-level parsing control.
capabilities.title: Tokenizer and tree construction

capabilities.text: Access specialized element classes such as HTMLInputElement, HTMLFormElement, HTMLTableElement, and many more with their interface-specific properties.
capabilities.title: HTML element APIs

capabilities.text: Serialize documents, fragments, or elements back to HTML strings using serialise, outer_html, or XMLSerializer.
capabilities.title: Serialization

limitations.text: CSS selector matching supports core Selectors Level 3 grammar; dynamic and legacy pseudo-classes raise NotImplementedError.
CSSRule.type and CSSRule.css_text are not implemented; concrete rule subclasses expose their own properties instead.
Form constraint validation and HTMLImageElement.decode are present on the API surface but not yet implemented.
The library builds internal layout structures but does not expose a public API for rendering to image or PDF.
JavaScript execution via JSContext requires the optional quickjs extra and exposes a read-only DOM proxy; dynamic import() is not implemented.
Single-colon legacy pseudo-element forms are not parsed by the CSS selector parser.

problems_solved.text: Enables parsing raw HTML strings or files into a standards-compliant DOM tree using the WHATWG tokenization and tree-construction algorithms.
Supports querying and mutating DOM nodes programmatically with element creation, attribute manipulation, and traversal helpers like TreeWalker and Range.
Resolves computed styles by attaching CSS stylesheets and applying cascade rules including specificity, inheritance, and !important.
Provides URL parsing and manipulation, query-string editing, and byte-stream encoding detection for robust web content handling.

product_summary.text: Aspose.HTML FOSS for Python is an open-source Python library implementing a standards-based HTML parser, DOM tree, CSSOM, and serialization, with optional JavaScript execution via QuickJS.

uncertainties: The exact set of CSS pseudo-classes that raise NotImplementedError is not listed in the facts.
It is unclear whether the layout structures are used internally for any purpose beyond rendering, which is not yet exposed.
The scope of the 'read-only DOM proxy' in JSContext is not detailed beyond example:006.
It is not specified whether the tokenizer and tree builder are fully compliant with the latest WHATWG HTML Standard.
The behavior of detect_encoding when multiple conflicting encodings are detected is not described.
The exact conditions under which tests for JSContext and Skia are skipped are only partially described in the inherited README.
It is unclear whether HTMLDocument.load supports loading from URLs or only local paths.
The compatibility guarantees for public symbols beyond those listed in PUBLIC_API.md are not detailed in the facts.

workflows.name: Parse and modify HTML
workflows.text: Parse an HTML string with HTMLDocument.parse, create new elements with Document.create_element, append them to the DOM, and serialize the result with serialise.

workflows.name: Apply and inspect CSS
workflows.text: Attach a CSSStyleSheet to a Document, call Element.get_computed_style, and read resolved property values from ComputedStyleDeclaration.

workflows.name: Execute JavaScript against DOM
workflows.text: Create a JSContext with a Document, evaluate JavaScript strings, and access DOM properties through a read-only proxy.

workflows.name: Tokenize HTML directly
workflows.text: Instantiate Tokenizer with an HTML string, call tokenize(), and inspect tokens such as StartTagToken and CharacterToken.

workflows.name: Work with URLs and query parameters
workflows.text: Construct a URL, access or modify search_params, and serialize the updated URL to a string.

workflows.name: Detect character encoding
workflows.text: Pass byte data to detect_encoding to infer encoding, confidence, and decoded text using BOM and meta-charset sniffing.
